en: Sutta Nipāta 5.12 The Young Man Jaṭukaṇṇi’s Question “Having heard of the Hero who is free from desire, I have come.”
"Thus spoke the Venerable Jatukaṇṇī:
'One who has come desiring to ask about the crossing of the flood—
O Sahajanetta, speak of the state of peace.'"
Tell me this as it truly is, O Blessed One: for the Blessed One, having overcome sensual desires,
moves about like the sun, radiant with its splendor, shining over the earth.
O you of vast wisdom, explain to me, who am of limited wisdom,
that Dhamma by which I may understand the complete relinquishing of birth and aging in this world.
“Remove greed for sensual pleasures,
Jatukaṇṇī,” said the Blessed One,
“seeing renunciation as security.”
Whether acquired or relinquished,
let there be nothing whatsoever for you.
Dry up that which was in the past.
Let there be nothing for you in the future;
if you do not grasp at anything in the middle,
you will wander in peace.
For one who is entirely free from craving for name-and-form, O Brahmin,
no taints exist within him.
"By these one falls into the power of Death.
This was the eleventh inquiry of the young brahmin Jaṭukaṇṇī.
